subject: ct-02: Cross-exam answer pattern audit -- Q3 absolute value pattern
body:
## Cross-Exam Answer Pattern Audit: RP1-RP7

Date: 2026-02-24
Auditor: GD
Method: Programmatic analysis of correct_answer fields across all questions in RP1-RP7

### Summary

Simple numeric answers (1-6, -1 to -6) appear frequently across exams -- this is expected for algebra (many problems share the same numeric answers). Not a concern by itself.

### Pattern Flag: Q3 Always Identifies Absolute Value Parent Function

Every Q3 in RP1-RP7 follows this pattern:
- Standard: W2.b
- Type: identify
- First input: parent function dropdown -- correct answer is ALWAYS 'absolute value'

Evidence:
- RP1 Q3: absolute value, -3, 5
- RP2 Q3: absolute value, 2, -8
- RP3 Q3: absolute value, 9, -1
- RP4 Q3: absolute value, 2, 4, -6
- RP5 Q3: absolute value, 4, -3, -8
- RP6 Q3: absolute value, 4, 2, -12
- RP7 Q3: absolute value, 2, 3, -4

### Risk Assessment

If Kai takes more than 2 exams, he can detect the Q3 pattern and answer 'absolute value' without doing the math. The x-intercept values vary (good) but the parent function is constant (pattern).

This is exactly the cross-exam memorization risk documented in exam verification protocol.

### Recommended Fix

Variate Q3 across exams. Suggested mix for RP1-RP10:
- RP1, RP4, RP7: absolute value (keep some)
- RP2, RP5, RP8: quadratic
- RP3, RP6, RP9: square root (or linear)
- RP10: linear or exponential

Alternatively: move W2.b absolute value questions to different positions in each exam (Q3 in RP1, Q7 in RP2, Q11 in RP3, etc.) so the pattern isn't position-detectable.

### Priority

Normal. Not an urgent bug -- Kai would need to have taken 3+ exams to detect this. But worth fixing before RP8-RP10 are published. Bundle with next GR content batch.

### No Other Hard Patterns Found

No other question positions showed >50% answer overlap across exams. The Q3 absolute value pattern is the only structural memorization risk detected in RP1-RP7.
